transcription.source: cipher runs of stamps 0001-0014 transcribed sign by sign under the doc. 169 key (texts/R9957_runs_A/B/C.md, 23 Oct 2026); the contemporary decipherment of stamps 0017-0018 (texts/R9957_decifrado_f274.txt). system.summary: R9957: the Isabella-Charles V cipher of 1535-38 (AGS Estado leg. 1.1.1 doc. 169, per Luo 2021 and Tomokiyo): homophonic letters, double letters, syllables as base sign plus vowel stroke or numbers 32-91, codes 92-211, nulls.
system.notes: System description taken from Tomokiyo's summary of Luo (2021), not rebuilt here. R9952 uses the Charles V-Prince Philip cipher (Tomokiyo).

prior_solution.where: R9957: Luo 2021 (thesis, Universitat de Valencia) p. 287, key AGS Estado leg. 1.1.1 doc. 169; partial contemporary decipherment on the leaves. R9952: contemporary marginal and separate decipherment; key matched by Tomokiyo (cryptiana).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: DECODE metadata for R9952/R9957 via the API; 38 images fetched with the shared cookie.
Viewed all pages: R9952 is a different letter (Cremona 1543), deciphered in the margins and on ff. 13-14.
Two subagents transcribed the R9957 cipher passages, pp. 1-9 and 10-18.
Found the contemporary decipherment of the pp. 16-17 cipher on pp. 17-18 and two interlinear glosses on p. 16; read the decipherment.
Hard-EM monotone aligner (from balbases1677) of the p. 16-17 tokens against the decipherment.
Tomokiyo cryptiana page (cached copy) lists R9957 as deciphered and printed in Luo 2021 p. 287, cipher AGS Estado leg. 1.1.1 doc. 169, and R9952 as deciphered in the margin.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R9957: the first-pass transcriptions (trans_p1-9.txt, trans_p10-18.txt), Luo's 2021 decipherment linked through cryptiana (modern, not copied); R9952: no transcription or decryption in the repository (contemporary decipherment on the images only).

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): R9957 is in the repository only as fragments of its contemporary decipherment (Luo's print not copied); R9952 has no text at all. Both relabelled decoded, not read; class kept already solved (R9957 printed by Luo 2021).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b18): the DECODE record pages of R9952 and R9957 list page images only (20 and 18), no transcription, plaintext, key or comments; all 38 images (main checkout img/) opened. R9952: the full contemporary decipherment is on images P12-P18, P20 (ff. 13-14 bis). R9957: the contemporary decipherment of the last cipher passage is on stamps 0017-0018. Luo's thesis PDF (key doc. 169 pp. 603-606, edition pp. 287-290) was already in the main checkout (caracciolo1537/prior/luo2021.pdf); RODERIC now answers with an Anubis bot check and was not used.

R9952: the decipherment on ff. 13-14 bis transcribed line by line (texts/R9952_decifrado_ff13-14.txt, 1,919 words); it gives only the ciphered passages, marking each return to clear with '/ lo otro claro /'.

R9952: decipherment checked against the figures of ff. 10-12 (images P5, P6, P9, P11): every clear word or phrase left inside the cipher runs falls in the same order and place, and Tomokiyo's code words (go para, pi enemigo, xu dinero) stand where the decipherment has those words. One difference: figures 'dexandolo', decipherer 'dexando'. Not checked sign by sign: no key of this cipher in the repository.

R9957: the key AGS Estado leg. 1.1.1 doc. 169 summarised from Luo's images (texts/R9957_key169.md): letters with up to three homophones, syllables as base sign + vowel mark (underline a, + e, # i, p o, o u) or the numbers 32-91, codes 92-211 and graphic signs, dotted signs and numbers from 212 null. Calibrated on stamp 0001: 'se gra[?] e de manera que no se pierda'; a plain a = e, underlined a = da.

R9957: the 52 cipher runs of stamps 0001-0014 read sign by sign on crops at 1.6-2.4x native resolution under the doc. 169 key, in three parts (texts/R9957_runs_A.md 0001-0006, _B.md 0007-0011, _C.md 0012-0014), each with its sign transcription, decode and comparison with Luo; about 1,600 words. Key observations (none changed): e+ like a hooked 4, ŧ̲ like ŧ+, the nn sign = ñ, 28 for initial r, L# = zi, dotted signs null. Recorded, not adopted: dinero with 52 on 0005-0006 and 53 on 0007-0014; 5 for b three times (key d); a sign 7° (a[?yu]da, cu[?yo]).

R9957: run B16 (stamp 0009, about 14 signs: a# L+ 68 1 L ep ·64 4 ŧ# 31 U 9̲ | 50 ŧ+ n ep) gives no sentence under the key; Luo prints no cipher at this place. The two dense blocks on stamp 0011 (B25, B28) only partly carried; two figures on 0013 ([43], [6]) with no value.

R9957: the contemporary decipherment of the last cipher passage (stamps 0017-0018) transcribed line by line (texts/R9957_decifrado_f274.txt); the cipher of stamps 0016-0017 not re-read sign by sign (the code 97, Antonio de Leyva, stands where the decipherment has 'Antonio').

R9957: decodes compared with Luo 2021 pp. 287-290 run by run (her edition used only as a check, cited not copied): agreement in substance throughout; 14 places where the figures differ are followed (e.g. 'En lo de los cinco mil' for her 'En los', 'pongo' for 'ponpo', 'asientos de trezientos' for 'asi en todo de', 'me embien' for 'ma (sic.) enbien'); 'Gonçalo de Ayora' (stamp 0005) is cipher that she prints as clear.

Readings and translations written (texts/R9952_reading.md, R9957_reading.md, _en.md; log texts/R9952-R9957_reread_log.md), each aligned word by word with its source (b18_align.py: R9952 1,917/1,919 words carried by the decipherment, R9957 all reading words carried by the run decodes, the clear words around them and the f. 274r decipherment). Clean-sentence share of the reading bodies: R9952 0.683 (1.00 on explicit holes), R9957 0.629 (0.953). Both set read (grade B).

texts.label: Charles V to the Empress Isabella, Borgo San Donnino, 17 May 1536
texts.summary: Charles V, on his way north from Rome, writes to the Empress Isabella with long cipher passages on Spain's frontier defences and the coming war with France: 25-30,000 German troops for Italy, more raised in Germany and Flanders, the Count of Nassau entering France from the Luxembourg side, and the diversion of the French King's forces. The full decipherment is Wanruo Luo's, printed in her thesis El lenguaje cifrado de Isabel de Portugal (1530-1539) (Universitat de València 2021) p. 287 with the key AGS Estado leg. 1.1.1 doc. 169; cryptiana spanish2C cites it.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b18): the cipher runs of ff. 270r-273v read sign by sign from the DECODE images under the key AGS Estado leg. 1.1.1 doc. 169 (as reproduced by Luo 2021, pp. 603-606; texts/R9957_key169.md), sign transcriptions and decodes in texts/R9957_runs_A/B/C.md; the last passage (ff. 273v-274r) from its contemporary decipherment on f. 274r (texts/R9957_decifrado_f274.txt). Luo's edition (pp. 287-290, in copyright) used only as a check, cited not copied; 14 places where the figures differ from her text are followed. Reading body 0.629 clean sentences on _check_reading.py, 0.953 on explicit holes (the word list lacks the period spelling). Open: a tear and one unreadable group in run 1, run B16 (about 14 signs on stamp 0009, no sentence), parts of the dense blocks on stamp 0011, a faded fold on 0013.

texts.label: Charles V to Prince Philip, Cremona, 19 Jun 1543
texts.summary: Charles V to Prince Philip on the Farnese offer through the Marqués del Vasto: two million ducats and a yearly census for the investiture of Milan for Ottavio Farnese, Duke of Camerino. Deciphered at the time in the margins of ff. 10-12 and in full on ff. 13-14.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b18): the contemporary decipherment on ff. 13-14 bis ('del Emperador a Su Al.') transcribed line by line (texts/R9952_decifrado_ff13-14.txt) and checked against the figures of ff. 10-12: every clear word left inside the cipher runs and Tomokiyo's code words (go para, pi enemigo, xu dinero) stand in the same order and place; one disagreement (figures 'dexandolo', decipherer 'dexando'), the figures followed. No key of this cipher in the repository, so the runs between the clear words are not checked sign by sign. Reading body 0.683 clean sentences, 1.00 on explicit holes.
